instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires periodic expense statements to be filed by registered principals (not lobbyists) on set dates, and does not impose an annual lobbyist-filed spending report.
Expense statements are required semiannually from principals, and no monthly lobbyist-filed spending report is created in the provided provisions.
The reporting obligation shown is a principal’s semiannual expense statement and licensing/authorization requirements, not any other-frequency lobbyist spending report.
The only periodic spending report in the text is the principal’s expense statement due July 31 and January 31, not quarterly lobbyist reports.
Wisconsin requires every registered principal to file semiannual expense statements; it does not name the lobbyist as the filer of a separate semiannual spending report.
The statute sets fixed semiannual due dates for principal expense statements and contains no tri-annual lobbyist spending report cadence.
Itemized expense disclosure is required in a principal’s expense statement, but lobbyists are not the named filers of a separate spending report.
The requirement to report legislative proposals/topics is imposed on principals as a condition of lobbying by/for the principal, not as a lobbyist-filed spending/activity report.
Compensation to lobbyists must be included in the principal’s reported lobbying expenditures, but the statute does not require lobbyists themselves to disclose earnings in a separate report.
The required record is of time spent and activities (e.g., meeting with officials) by the principal, not a lobbyist-filed disclosure of contacts.
Issue/topic time proportions are reported by the principal, and there is no requirement that lobbyists file expenditures per issue.
Reporting of topics/legislative proposals is a principal reporting obligation; the statute does not create a lobbyist-filed issue disclosure report.
The statute requires the principal to report legislative proposals/rules/topics, not the lobbyist as the filer of an activity report.

Although the principal’s statement covers categories including travel/living expenses and reimbursements, there is no lobbyist-filed spending report requiring disclosure of gifts/entertainment/transportation/lodging.
Indirect and overhead costs are addressed in the principal’s expense statement, but lobbyists are not required to file their own spending report disclosing indirect costs.

The statute requires principals (not lobbyists) to file expense statements including lobbying expenditures; therefore lobbyists are not required to file itemized spending reports with compensation and bill numbers.
A lobbyist license application may include the address of the applicant’s primary residence, but the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose address/phone in a periodic spending report.
Legislative proposal/topic identification is a principal reporting duty; lobbyists are not required to file an activity report identifying bills/actions.
Disclosure of a principal’s business activity/nature is required in the principal’s registration statement, not in a lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.

The principal’s registration statement specifies the principal’s name and business address, but the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose principals’ address/phone in a lobbyist spending report.
Lobbyist authorization is filed (by the lobbyist or principal) per principal, but there is no lobbyist-filed periodic spending report requiring disclosure of all principals represented.
Bill/proposed rule identification is reported by the principal to the commission, not by lobbyists in a separate spending report.
Direct lobbying costs such as compensation to lobbyists are included in the principal’s aggregate lobbying expenditures, but lobbyists are not required to file their own disclosure report.
Total lobbying expenditures are reported by the principal on its expense statement; the statute does not impose a lobbyist-filed total expenditure report.
No provision requires lobbyists to file itemized spending reports including employer, issues, bill numbers, and compensation; those disclosures, where present, occur on the principal’s filings.
The statute’s periodic filing requirement applies to principals’ expense statements and does not require lobbyists to file 'no activity' reports for periods with no spending.
The expense statement requirements do not include reporting of lobbyist spending on household members of public officials, and there is no lobbyist spending report requirement.
While the principal’s report includes some itemization (e.g., listing lobbyist name/address when payments exceed $200), the statute does not require a lobbyist-filed itemized spending report.

unscoreable_emissions.justification: No lobbyist-filed periodic spending report is specified, so there is no 'other' reporting frequency to describe.
